sources.title: A shortage of ore is causing a pricing revolution in copper
evidence: The decades-old system that the copper industry uses to price mined ores is fracturing in the face of an acute shortage.
the number of deals linked to the benchmark price has already fallen sharply, and is set to drop further next year
Less than 30% of China’s copper concentrates trade has been linked to the benchmark this year
On a global scale, CRU expects some 45% of concentrate sales to remain linked to the benchmark
Miners and smelters are set to meet again for crunch talks during a major industry gathering in Shanghai next week

sources.title: EU launches expiry review of anti-dumping duties on MEG imports from US and Saudi Arabia
evidence: The European Comission has launched an expiry review of anti-dumping duties on monoethylene glycol (MEG) imports
from the US and Saudi Arabia which were originally set to expire on 16 November.
The investigation, which was announced on 13 November, will consider whether the situation of companies producing
The investigation should be concluded within 12 months of initiation
the deadline may be extended up to 15 months.
Existing anti-dumping measures shall remain in force, pending the outcome of the review.
MEG has been subject to ADDs since 2021 when the EU imposed a flat duty of 7.7% on imports from Saudi Arabia
a range of 3% to 60% on US companies, with the lowest rate of 3% applied to major producer Lotte Chemical.
MEG is primarily used in the production of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) resin polyester fibers and films.

sources.title: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover, IEA says
evidence: The world oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year
as Middle East exports recover faster than global oil demand despite continued attacks on shipping.
Oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter
1.7 million bpd higher than forecast demand.
The IEA had previously forecast a fourth-quarter supply deficit.
World oil demand is forecast to fall by 2.7 million bpd in 2026 to 102.3 million bpd
For 2027, the IEA sees the supply surplus at about 3.8 million bpd
